train.role: Thresholds use only this window, expanding, then freeze.

test.role: Factor rules were scored once and not changed. The overlay stack was chosen on this window once.

parameters.rebalance: monthly, own last session of the month
parameters.execution: signal at the close, new position earns the next session, cost charged on the signal day

data.prices: Yahoo Finance daily continuous front-month futures, plus cash index and GLD for the roll check.
data.real_yield: U.S. Treasury H.15 10-year inflation-indexed yield. This is the series FRED publishes as DFII10. The FRED file download did not respond; the Treasury file is the primary source.

citations.cite: Moskowitz, Tobias J., Yao Hua Ooi, and Lasse Heje Pedersen. "Time Series Momentum." Journal of Financial Economics 104, no. 2 (2012): 228–250.
citations.used_for: 12-month sign, the average of 1/3/6/12 month signs, and sign times target-vol over forecast-vol.

citations.cite: Asness, Clifford S., Tobias J. Moskowitz, and Lasse Heje Pedersen. "Value and Momentum Everywhere." Journal of Finance 68, no. 3 (2013): 929–985.
citations.used_for: Futures value as the sign of the negative five-year return.

citations.cite: Koijen, Ralph S. J., Tobias J. Moskowitz, Lasse Heje Pedersen, and Evert B. Vrugt. "Carry." Journal of Financial Economics 127, no. 1 (2018): 197–225.
citations.used_for: Carry as the sign of the futures basis versus cash. Gold uses a real-yield proxy because the deferred contract is not in the free history.

citations.cite: Erb, Claude B., and Campbell R. Harvey. "The Golden Dilemma." Financial Analysts Journal 69, no. 4 (2013): 10–42.
citations.used_for: Gold's opportunity cost tracked with the 10-year real Treasury yield. Long gold when that yield is negative.

citations.cite: Moreira, Alan, and Tyler Muir. "Volatility-Managed Portfolios." Journal of Finance 72, no. 4 (2017): 1611–1644.
citations.used_for: Scale exposure by the inverse of recent realized volatility. The regime filter is the coarse version: flat above the training-era 80th percentile.

citations.cite: Barroso, Pedro, and Pedro Santa-Clara. "Momentum Has Its Moments." Journal of Financial Economics 116, no. 1 (2015): 111–120.
citations.used_for: Why the momentum sleeve is cut in a high-volatility state. The paper scales by the volatility of the momentum strategy; the filter here is the simpler on/off rule.

citations.cite: Maillard, Sébastien, Thierry Roncalli, and Jérôme Teiletche. "The Properties of Equally Weighted Risk Contribution Portfolios." Journal of Portfolio Management 36, no. 4 (2010): 60–70.
citations.used_for: Equal risk contribution. With a common correlation assumption this is inverse-volatility weighting, applied here as an equal dollar-vol budget per market.

citations.cite: Kuttner, Kenneth N. "Monetary Policy Surprises and Interest Rates: Evidence from the Fed Funds Futures Market." Journal of Monetary Economics 47, no. 3 (2001): 523–544.
citations.used_for: The FOMC surprise is the change in the front 30-day fed-funds future on the statement day. A free Reuters poll of the decision does not exist for the full sample.

citations.cite: Boyd, John H., Jian Hu, and Ravi Jagannathan. "The Stock Market's Reaction to Unemployment News: Why Bad News Is Usually Good for Stocks." Journal of Finance 60, no. 2 (2005): 649–672.
citations.used_for: The payroll surprise flips sign with the growth state. In an expansion a strong print is a short in the equity indexes; in a contraction it is a long.

citations.cite: Baker, Scott R., Nicholas Bloom, and Steven J. Davis. "Measuring Economic Policy Uncertainty." Quarterly Journal of Economics 131, no. 4 (2016): 1593–1636.
citations.used_for: The news layer is their daily news-based Economic Policy Uncertainty index, lagged one month, used only to flatten equity-index futures.

layers.selection_rule: Of the pre-specified stacks, keep the one with the highest out-of-sample net dollar P&L after costs, if that P&L is above the volatility-filtered trend alone. If none is above it, keep the trend. A tie keeps the earlier stack. The naive card is the benchmark and is not a candidate. The test window is used for this choice once.

core.summary: Volatility-filtered trend, one contract. The base layer.

hit_rate.note: Sign hit on the event session, absolute return at least 5 basis points, NQ/ES/GC/CL only. This is not the six-asset basket in the accuracy report.

sources.cpi_nfp: Philadelphia Fed Real-Time Data Set, monthly vintages PCPI and EMPLOY. First vintage that contains the observation month. Month-over-month CPI uses that vintage's own prior level. Payrolls are the change in thousands in that vintage.
sources.fomc: Federal Reserve statement pages whose title contains 'FOMC statement'. Surprise is the change in the Yahoo ZQ=F implied rate (100 minus the price). On a session dated the 1st, 2nd or 3rd the change is open to close, because the continuous contract splices then. Otherwise it is close to close.
sources.news: Baker, Bloom and Davis daily news-based US EPU, averaged within the calendar month. policyuncertainty.com All_Daily_Policy_Data.csv. This is the series FRED publishes as USEPUINDXD. The FRED file did not download.
sources.consensus: No free CPI, payroll or funds-rate survey history was available. CPI and payroll consensus is the median of the previous 36 first releases. FOMC consensus is the rate already in the fed-funds future.
